symptom: PC1 cannot reach Server1 in VLAN 30
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick topology; Gi0/0.10 = VLAN 10, Gi0/0.30 = VLAN 30
show_outputs: GigabitEthernet0/0.10 is up, line protocol is up | GigabitEthernet0/0.30 is administratively down, line protocol is down
expected_fault: Gi0/0.30 administratively down - needs 'no shutdown'

symptom: PC2 cannot reach any external website
topology_note: Router1 configured with NAT overload for inside VLAN 20 to ISP interface Gi0/1
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: (empty) | show run (partial): interface GigabitEthernet0/1 ip nat outside | interface Vlan20 (no ip nat inside statement present)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip nat inside' on Vlan20 interface

symptom: PC3 cannot ping its default gateway despite correct IP configuration
topology_note: PC3 connects via straight-through cable to Switch1 Fa0/3, uplinked to Router1 Fa0/0
show_outputs: FastEthernet0/3 is up, line protocol is down (not connect) | show interfaces status: Fa0/3 notconnect auto auto
expected_fault: Physical layer issue - bad cable, wrong port, or duplex/speed mismatch on Fa0/3

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 30 on Switch2 cannot reach Server1 even though interface is up
topology_note: Switch2 access port Fa0/5 assigned VLAN 30; router sub-interface Gi0/0.30 configured with 'encapsulation dot1Q 20'
show_outputs: show vlan brief (Switch2): VLAN0030 active Fa0/5 | show run (Router1): interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30 encapsulation dot1Q 20
expected_fault: VLAN mismatch - sub-interface encapsulated for VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 30

symptom: Server1 (VLAN 30) can be pinged from PC1 but SSH connection is refused
topology_note: ACL 110 applied inbound on Router1 Gi0/0.30 to control access to Server1
show_outputs: show access-lists 110: 10 permit icmp any host 192.168.30.10 | 20 deny ip any any (implicit/explicit) - no permit tcp eq 22 entry present
expected_fault: Missing 'permit tcp any host 192.168.30.10 eq 22' entry in ACL 110

symptom: OSPF neighbors on Router1 and Router2 are not forming an adjacency
topology_note: Both routers configured for OSPF area 0 on the 10.0.12.0/30 link
show_outputs: show run (Router1): router ospf 1 network 10.0.12.0 255.255.255.252 area 0 | show ip ospf neighbor: (empty)
expected_fault: Wildcard mask used instead of inverse mask - should be 0.0.0.3 not 255.255.255.252

symptom: PC4 can reach all internal VLANs but not the internet
topology_note: Router1 has static routes to internal subnets but no route to ISP
show_outputs: show ip route: 192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected | 192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected | (no 0.0.0.0/0 gateway of last resort entry)
expected_fault: Missing default route 'ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <isp-next-hop>'

symptom: Trunk between Switch1 and Switch2 is not passing VLAN 40 traffic
topology_note: Switch1 Gi0/1 configured as trunk; Switch2 Gi0/1 configured as access port
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk (Switch1): Gi0/1 lists as trunk, allowed vlans 1,10,20,30,40 | show interfaces switchport (Switch2): Gi0/1 Administrative Mode: static access
expected_fault: Switch2 Gi0/1 set to access mode instead of trunk - needs 'switchport mode trunk'

symptom: Two hosts on the same VLAN intermittently lose connectivity and show duplicate IP warnings
topology_note: PC5 and Server2 both configured with static IP addressing on VLAN 20
show_outputs: PC5: IP Address 192.168.20.50 | Server2 show run int Vlan20-equivalent: ip address 192.168.20.50 255.255.255.0 | Windows event log: 'Duplicate IP address detected'
expected_fault: Duplicate static IP 192.168.20.50 assigned to both PC5 and Server2

symptom: Internal hosts can reach some external sites but NAT translations disappear intermittently
topology_note: Router1 configured with NAT overload but access-list reference is incorrect
show_outputs: show run (partial): ip nat inside source list 5 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload | access-list 5 permit 192.168.10.0 (missing wildcard mask, defaults to host route)
expected_fault: access-list 5 missing wildcard mask - only matches host 192.168.10.0, not the subnet

symptom: Redundant link between Switch1 and Switch3 is unexpectedly unused, no load balancing
topology_note: Two switches connected via two trunk links for redundancy, STP running default settings
show_outputs: show spanning-tree vlan 10: Gi0/2 role Altn state BLK | Gi0/1 role Root state FWD
expected_fault: Expected behavior - STP is blocking Gi0/2 to prevent a loop; not a fault but often misread as one

symptom: New hosts on VLAN 50 are not receiving IP addresses via DHCP
topology_note: DHCP server is centrally located on Router1; VLAN 50 is a remote subnet via Switch3
show_outputs: show run int Vlan50 (Switch3, L3 switch): no ip helper-address configured | client shows IP 169.254.x.x (APIPA)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address <dhcp-server-ip>' on VLAN 50 interface

symptom: PC6 in VLAN 40 has no connectivity, interface LEDs show no link light
topology_note: Router sub-interface Gi0/0.40 serves VLAN 40 for the finance department
show_outputs: GigabitEthernet0/0.40 is administratively down, line protocol is down
expected_fault: Gi0/0.40 administratively down - needs 'no shutdown'

symptom: Connection between Switch1 and Router1 is up but experiencing high error rates and slow throughput
topology_note: Switch1 Fa0/1 set to 100/full; Router1 Fa0/0 left at auto-negotiate
show_outputs: show interfaces Fa0/1 (Switch1): 100Mb/s, full-duplex | show interfaces Fa0/0 (Router1): 10Mb/s, half-duplex, %input errors, collisions
expected_fault: Duplex/speed mismatch - Router1 Fa0/0 auto-negotiated incorrectly against a fixed peer

symptom: VLAN 60 traffic is not passing across the Switch2-Switch4 trunk despite trunk being up
topology_note: Trunk configured on both ends but allowed VLAN list was restricted during initial setup
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk (Switch2): Gi0/2 allowed vlans: 1,10,20,30,40,50 (VLAN 60 missing from list)
expected_fault: VLAN 60 missing from trunk allowed list - needs 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 60'

symptom: OSPF is only advertising part of the expected network on Router2
topology_note: Router2 configured to advertise 172.16.4.0/22 network into OSPF area 0
show_outputs: show run (Router2): router ospf 1 network 172.16.4.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
expected_fault: Wildcard mask 0.0.0.255 only covers a /24, not the intended /22 (should be 0.0.3.255)

symptom: Branch office subnet 192.168.99.0/24 is unreachable from HQ
topology_note: Static route configured on HQ router pointing to branch router
expected_fault: Static route has a typo - 192.168.9.0 instead of 192.168.99.0

symptom: PC7 connected to Switch2 Fa0/8 cannot get past the switch onto the trunk, isolated from network
topology_note: Switch2 Fa0/8 was previously used for an inter-switch link and left in trunk mode
show_outputs: show interfaces switchport (Switch2 Fa0/8): Administrative Mode: trunk | Operational Mode: trunk
expected_fault: Port Fa0/8 left in trunk mode - needs 'switchport mode access' plus correct VLAN assignment

symptom: Two router interfaces on Router1 both show 'up/up' but neither can reach expected next hops
topology_note: Gi0/0 and Gi0/1 were configured during initial setup, both intended for different subnets
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: GigabitEthernet0/0 10.0.1.1 up up | GigabitEthernet0/1 10.0.1.1 up up
expected_fault: Both Gi0/0 and Gi0/1 configured with the same IP address 10.0.1.1

symptom: Internal hosts on VLAN 70 cannot access the internet, no NAT translations are created
topology_note: NAT configured for VLAN 10/20 but VLAN 70 was added later without updating NAT ACL
show_outputs: show run: access-list 5 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 | access-list 5 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 (no entry for 192.168.70.0/24)
expected_fault: access-list 5 missing a permit entry for the VLAN 70 subnet 192.168.70.0/24

symptom: Switch3 unexpectedly became the STP root bridge for VLAN 10, causing suboptimal traffic paths
topology_note: Switch1 was intended to be root bridge but had its priority changed during troubleshooting and never reverted
show_outputs: show spanning-tree vlan 10: Switch3 Bridge ID Priority 4096 | Switch1 Bridge ID Priority 32768 (default)
expected_fault: Switch3 has a lower (better) priority than intended root bridge Switch1

symptom: New hosts on VLAN 20 stop receiving DHCP addresses during peak hours
topology_note: DHCP pool for VLAN 20 was sized for the original 20 hosts; department has grown to 45
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool VLAN20: Current index 192.168.20.255 | Total addresses 30 | Leased addresses 30
expected_fault: DHCP pool exhausted - only 30 addresses defined for /24 network segment now needing more

symptom: PC8 in the guest VLAN 80 has no connectivity after a router maintenance window
topology_note: Router sub-interface Gi0/0.80 for guest VLAN was disabled during maintenance and not re-enabled
show_outputs: GigabitEthernet0/0.80 is administratively down, line protocol is down
expected_fault: Gi0/0.80 administratively down - needs 'no shutdown'

symptom: Devices on the native VLAN are experiencing intermittent connectivity issues and CDP native VLAN mismatch warnings
topology_note: Switch1 trunk native VLAN set to 1; Switch2 trunk native VLAN set to 99
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk (Switch1): Native VLAN 1 | show interfaces trunk (Switch2): Native VLAN 99 | %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH log message
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch between trunk ends - both sides must match (e.g., both set to 1 or both to 99)

symptom: Server1 in VLAN 30 is unreachable from all VLANs, but was reachable before an ACL update
topology_note: ACL 110 was recently modified and reapplied to the router sub-interface
show_outputs: show run: interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30 ip access-group 110 out | ACL 110 was written to filter traffic entering the subinterface, not leaving it
expected_fault: ACL 110 applied 'out' when it was designed to filter inbound traffic - should be 'ip access-group 110 in'

symptom: OSPF adjacency between Router2 and Router3 flaps up and down repeatedly
topology_note: Point-to-point link between Router2 and Router3 on 10.0.23.0/30
concept_tag: incorrect wildcard mask / mismatched network statement
show_outputs: show run (Router3): router ospf 1 network 10.0.23.0 0.0.0.7 area 0
expected_fault: Wildcard mask 0.0.0.7 covers a /29, mismatched with the /30 link, causing intermittent adjacency issues

symptom: All hosts on VLAN 90 lost connectivity to other VLANs after switch reload
topology_note: VLAN 90 is a routed SVI (switch virtual interface) on a Layer 3 switch
show_outputs: show run int Vlan90: no ip address configured | show ip interface brief: Vlan90 unassigned administratively down down
expected_fault: SVI Vlan90 lost its IP address configuration after reload - needs 'ip address <addr> <mask>' re-applied

symptom: Voice VLAN phones are registering intermittently and losing QoS markings
topology_note: Switch access ports configured with a data VLAN but voice VLAN command omitted
show_outputs: show interfaces switchport (Fa0/10): Voice VLAN: none | Access Mode VLAN: 10 (data)
expected_fault: Missing 'switchport voice vlan <id>' command on access ports used by IP phones

symptom: NAT translations stop being created once approximately 250 internal hosts are active simultaneously
topology_note: NAT overload configured using a single outside interface IP address
show_outputs: show ip nat statistics: Total active translations: 0 (max reached, prior peak ~64000 exceeded due to session churn) | Outside interface: GigabitEthernet0/1 (single public IP)
expected_fault: Single-IP NAT overload nearing port exhaustion under heavy simultaneous session load

symptom: After enabling portfast on a port later connected to another switch, the network experienced a broadcast storm
topology_note: Switch1 Fa0/12 was configured with portfast for a workstation, later repurposed as an uplink to Switch5 without removing portfast
show_outputs: show run int Fa0/12: spanning-tree portfast | show interfaces Fa0/12: connected device MAC table shows switch BPDUs arriving on a portfast-enabled port
expected_fault: Portfast left enabled on a port now uplinked to another switch, bypassing STP loop prevention
